newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - April 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - April 29.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on April 29:

WASHINGTON - The Supreme Court made it tougher for victims of police brutality to successfully sue local governments, holding that a municipality cannot be held liable for an officer's actions even if he had a history of assault before being hired.
WASHINGTON - Former presidential candidate and Senate majority leader Bob Dole is out of the Senate, but still wielding a great deal of influence.
WASHINGTON - An emergency school trustee board voted on late Monday to close 11 public schools in the nation's capital, prompting angry and emotional reactions by many parents.
WASHINGTON - Political leaders in Prince Georges County face painful choices after voters approved one of the nation's toughest tax caps in November.

WASHINGTON - The U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations, Bill Richardson, was dispatched to Zaire to tell President Mobutu Sese Seko to step down and that Washington will help arrange a dignified exit, diplomatic sources said.

WASHINGTON - A wealthy Sudanese businessman helped raise over $500,000 for the Democratic National Committee last year and is not seeking to further his business interest through changes in U.S. policy toward Islamic countries like Sudan.
WASHINGTON - Many large Japanese companies are now declaring "no overtime" days to help break the country's famous addiction to marathon work hours.
